Wudinna Rare Earth Purification Update
ANSTO radionuclide removal test work results provide credible pathway to an upgraded rare earth product
Cobra

, a South Australian mineral exploration and development company, is pleased to announce that initial testing aimed at supporting a forthcoming Scoping Study have yielded favourable results confirming the Company's potential to produce a higher purity, higher proportioned heavy rare earth product with reduced radionuclide concentrations.

The Australian Nuclear Scientific Technology Organisation ("ANSTO") applied its proprietary radionuclide removal technology1 as part of ANSTO's on-going support to Cobra's flowsheet development efforts for Wudinna. Indicative results from the preliminary test work indicate that, radium (as Ra-225) removal was greater than 97%, actinium (Ac) removal was up to 90%, and the concentration of lower-value lanthanum (La) was reduced by 1% to 30%.

Importantly, the test work also demonstrated that >90% of the higher value magnet and heavy rare earth elements were retained. Final recoveries and elemental deportment remain subject to confirmation through solid assays and complete solid-liquid mass balance.

These initial results indicate that the purification step has the potential to both reduce radionuclide concentrations and selectively remove a proportion of lower value lanthanum before final product precipitation. Importantly, this could increase the relative weighting of valuable magnet and heavy rare earths in Cobra's mixed rare earth carbonate ("MREC") product and reduce the volume of lower-value material presented to downstream separation.

Results build on previously reported test work demonstrating the removal of cerium from In Situ Recovery ("ISR") pregnant liquor. Together, the results provide a potential pathway to a cleaner, higher-value intermediate product, while the technical and economic benefits of process integration to mid-stream separation will be evaluated within engineering and scoping studies.
Rupert Verco, Managing Director of Cobra, commented:

"ANSTO's initial purification test work is an important step in defining how we can improve the quality of the product generated from the Wudinna REE project. The work demonstrates substantial removal of radium and actinium, while also selectively reducing lower-value lanthanum and retaining magnet and heavy rare earths that underpin product value.

This is the first stage of evaluating this purification step. We will now incorporate these results into engineering design and the Scoping Study, including optimisation of operating conditions and the overall economic contribution of the process.

The results provide a credible pathway towards producing an upgraded MREC with an enhanced relative weighting of magnet and heavy rare earth elements and significantly reduced radionuclide concentrations."
Next Steps
Further testing is underway at ANSTO designed to support engineering assessment and the Scoping Study process. Key work streams include:
·    Dissolving Cobra's MREC and applying ANSTO's proprietary purification technology. Test work completed - results are pending
·    Lixiviant optimisation - Groundwater adoption at lower molarity Ammonium Sulphate. Test work completed - results are pending
·    Resource recovery evaluation - 40+ diagnostic leach tests performed from samples across the mineralised footprints. - testwork in progress

·    Bench scale ISR trials from ore composites at the Boland and Head prospects that will utilise optimised lixiviant conditions defined in the above tests (utilising Boland groundwater) and inform the conditions to be used within the planned Small Scale Production Study - Sighter Column underway. Columns are being prepared
About the Wudinna Rare Earths Project

Cobra has discovered what it believes to be a unique, scalable instance where ionic rare earth elements - containing economically attractive grades of valuable heavy and magnet rare earths - occur in a permeable horizon confined between horizons of impermeable clay.

Bench scale ISR testing has confirmed that this mineralisation is amenable to ISR recovery techniques. ISR techniques are currently in use (and have been used successfully for decades) in geologically similar environments, to recover uranium in South Australia which maintains a well-established ISR regulatory system.

Cobra's ongoing mineral recovery test work is evaluating the technical and economic potential for ISR recovery of critical rare earth elements at Boland. Engineering design, further test work and Scoping Study assessment will determine the operating configuration, recovery assumptions and potential development economics.

Cobra Resources is advancing two South Australian critical minerals opportunities: the Wudinna ionic rare earth project and the Manna Hill Copper Project.

Appendix 1: Background information - the Wudinna Rare Earth Project and ISR
·    The Wuddina Rear Earths were discovered by Cobra in 2023. Mineralisation is ionically bound to clays and organics within palaeochannel sands within the Narlaby Palaeochannel
·    Mineralisation occurs within a permeable sand within an aquifer that is saltier than sea water and is confined by impermeable clays

·    ISR is executed through engineered drillhole arrays that allow the injection of mildly acidic ammonium or magnesium sulphate lixiviants, using the confining nature of the geology to direct and lower the acidity of the orebody. This low-cost process enables mines to operate profitably at lower grades and lower rates of recovery

·    Once REEs are mobile in solution in groundwater, it is also possible, from an engineering standpoint, to recover the solution to surface via extraction drillholes, without any need for excavation or ground disturbance
·    The capital costs of ISR mining are low as they involve no material movements and do not require traditional infrastructure to process ore - i.e. metals are recovered in solution
·    Ionic mineralisation is highly desirable owing to its high weighting of valuable HREOs and the cost-effective method in which REEs can be desorbed

·    Ionic REE mineralisation in China is mined in an in-situ manner that relies on gravity to permeate mineralisation. The style of ISR process is unconfined and cannot be controlled, increasing the risk for environmental degradation. This low-cost process has enabled China to dominate mine supply of HREOs, supplying over 90% globally

·    Confined aquifer ISR is successfully executed globally within the uranium industry, accounting for more than 60% of the world's uranium production. This style of ISR has temporary ground disturbance, and the ground waters are regenerated over time
·    Cobra is aiming to demonstrate the economic and environmental benefits of recovering ionic HREOs through the more environmentally aquifer controlled ISR - a world first for rare earths

·    ANSTO laboratories prepared ~80g samples for diagnostic leaches, a 443g sample for a slurry leach and a 660g sample for a column leach. Diagnostic and slurry leaching were carried out in baffled leach vessels equipped with an overhead stirrer and applying a 0.5 M (NH4)2SO4 lixiviant solution, adjusted to the select pH using H2SO4.
·    0.5 M H2SO4 was utilised to maintain the test pH for the duration of the test, if necessary. The acid addition was measured.
·    Thief liquor samples were taken periodically.
·    At the completion of each test, the final pH was measured, the slurry was vacuum filtered to separate the primary filtrate.
·    The thief samples and primary filtrate were analysed as follows:
o  ICP-MS for Ce, Dy, Er, Eu, Gd, Ho, La, Lu, Mn, Nd, Pb, Pr, Sc, Sm, Tb, Th, Tm, U, Y, Yb.
o  ICP-OES for Al, Ca, Fe, K, Mg, Mn, Na, Si.
·    The water wash was stored but not analysed.
·    Column leaching was carried out in horizontal leaching column. The column was pressurised with nitrogen to 6 bar and submerged in a temperature controlled bath.
·    A 0.5 M (NH4)2SO4 lixiviant solution, adjusted to the select pH using H2SO4 was fed to the column at a controlled flowrate.

·    PLS collected from the end of the column was weighed, the SH and pH measured and the free acid concentration determined by titration. Liquor samples were taken from the collected PLS and analysed as follows:
o  ICP-MS for Ce, Dy, Er, Eu, Gd, Ho, La, Lu, Mn, Nd, Pb, Pr, Sc, Sm, Tb, Th, Tm, U, Y, Yb.

Geology
·      Deposit type, geological setting and style of mineralisation.

·      Ionic REE mineralisation also occurs in and adjacent to the Garford formation clays and silty sands.

·      Benchtop metallurgy studies indicate ISR amenability of rare earths within the Pidinga Formation basal sands summarized in RNS 1285Q (16 December 2024)
·      Ionic REE mineralisation is confirmed through metallurgical desorption testing where high recoveries are achieved at benign acidities (pH4-3) at ambient temperature.
·      QEMSCAN and petrology analysis support REE ionic mineralisation, with little to no secondary phases identified.

·      Ionic REE mineralisation occurs in reduced clay intervals that contact both saprolite and permeable sand units. Mineralisation contains variable sand quantities that yield permeability and promote in-situ recovery potential
·      Mineralisation is located within a confined aquifer
